title: PaxHub - Migration to MongoDB - PNR PROCESSOR - Evaluation and Optimization Tuning (Spike)
description:
Given PNR Processor function invocation duration has increased following the deployment earlier this week as part of the MongoDB migration
When the team evaluates comparable pre-deployment and post-deployment telemetry and profiles the processing path
Then the contributors to the increased invocation duration are identified with supporting evidence or explicitly documented investigation gaps
And performance tuning opportunities are evaluated safely in NONPROD and prioritized recommendations are documented without compromising processing correctness or reliability

Context: After the recent PNR Processor deployment, function invocation duration became slower. This spike evaluates why duration increased and whether processor performance can be enhanced. Confirm the affected deployment version, time window, and environment rather than assuming the deployment is the root cause. Compare representative workloads, PNR payload sizes, warm and cold invocations, traffic/concurrency, and configuration before and after deployment. Examine processor execution stages, MongoDB operations and connection usage, dependency/network latency, resource utilization, retries, and logging/tracing overhead where evidence indicates a bottleneck. Use existing monitoring and sanitized diagnostics. Production observation must remain non-disruptive; profiling or tuning experiments belong in controlled NONPROD tests. Deliver an evidence-backed assessment, measured experiment outcomes, configuration/documentation recommendations, and prioritized follow-up implementation work where justified. Production tuning deployment is outside this spike. A finding that no safe or worthwhile optimization is available is an acceptable outcome when supported by evidence.
acceptanceCriteria:
Establish comparable invocation duration baselines
Given PNR Processor invocation duration increased after the recent deployment
When the affected version, environment, and pre-deployment and post-deployment measurement windows are reviewed
Then the assessment records invocation counts and available latency distributions such as median, p95, and p99 alongside throughput, failures, and resource metrics
And workload size, concurrency, configuration changes, and warm versus cold invocations are accounted for, with missing baseline data and comparison limitations stated explicitly.

Identify evidence-backed processing bottlenecks
Given representative processor telemetry and sanitized execution traces are available
When the team examines PNR Processor execution stages, MongoDB calls, connection reuse, dependency latency, resource usage, retry behavior, and instrumentation overhead
Then observed contributors to invocation duration are quantified and correlated with the deployment or workload changes where supported
And confirmed findings are distinguished from unproven hypotheses, with telemetry gaps and additional investigation needs documented when a root cause cannot be established.

Evaluate tuning hypotheses through controlled NONPROD experiments
Given profiling identifies plausible code, MongoDB query/index, client connection, concurrency, or runtime configuration tuning opportunities
When approved hypotheses are tested in NONPROD against representative repeatable workloads
Then before-and-after invocation duration, throughput, error rate, and resource consumption are recorded with the tested settings
And results are reproducible, processing outputs remain correct, and unsupported or ineffective hypotheses are documented rather than presented as improvements.

Assess resilience under invalid data and dependency failures
Given representative tests include invalid or large PNR payloads, MongoDB timeouts, dependency failures, and retry conditions
When the baseline processor and any tuning candidate are evaluated in NONPROD
Then error handling, timeouts, retry/backoff, and existing failure-recovery behavior remain safe and observable without introducing lost or duplicate processing
And no experiment destabilizes production, bypasses security controls, or exposes sensitive PNR data in diagnostics.

Document findings and proposed configuration or instrumentation updates
Given baseline analysis and NONPROD experiments are complete
When the spike report is published and reviewed with the team
Then it includes the deployment comparison, evidence, bottleneck assessment, tested settings, limitations, and any recommended code, configuration, MongoDB, monitoring, or operational documentation changes
And the report explains any missing telemetry and records an evidence-supported no-change conclusion when no safe or worthwhile optimization is identified.

Prioritize safe optimization follow-up work
Given measured findings identify potential PNR Processor improvements or additional investigation requirements
When recommendations are assessed with processor owners and impacted consumers
Then expected invocation duration benefits, processing correctness, downstream impact, reliability, resource/cost tradeoffs, risks, and validation criteria are documented and prioritized
And justified implementation work is recorded as follow-up backlog items with rollout and rollback considerations rather than implicitly deploying production changes within this spike.
